 Follow Alabama Teacher, 30, Accused of Selling Pills to Student and Having Firearm on School Property
 Michael Gioia Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:40 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Montgomery County Detention Facility An Alabama teacher is no longer employed after being accused of selling drugs to a student.
 Langston Carter , 30, was arrested on Thursday, October 22, and charged with possession of a firearm on school property, two counts of unlawful distribution of a controlled substance and first-degree possession of marijuana, NBC affiliate WSFA reported.
 According to the outlet, police were called to L.E.A.D. Academy, a charter school in Montgomery, where a student told authorities he obtained two pills from Carter.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Per court records, the pills contained 5 milligrams of oxycodone hydrochloride and 325 milligrams of acetaminophen.
 "Students were placed on an immediate lockdown issued by the Montgomery Police Department to ensure integrity of the investigation," a Facebook statement from the school read.
 WSFA reported that the student claimed he paid $10 for the pills, which Carter allegedly offered to sell to him on numerous occasions. The student was reportedly told to send money via Cash App to Carter's girlfriend, but he didn't have an account, so he asked another student to do so.
 Google Maps
 The pills were then allegedly given to the student in the classroom, according to court documents.
 Advertisement Advertisement In an update from the school shared Friday, October 23, on Facebook , it stated that the teacher was "terminated."
 "Upon learning of the incident, school administration responded immediately," the statement said. "The incident occurred during school dismissal. Parents were notified of the lockdown approximately 3:30 p.m., following the conclusion of the search. At no time during the lockdown were any scholars placed in danger."
 Court filings seen by WSFA said that a K-9 conducted an open-air sniff outside Carter's vehicle, and police opened the trunk to find 6.9 grams of marijuana, mushroom-infused gummies, additional pills and a handgun, among other items.
 "We understand the concerns this incident has raised among our parents and school community," the school said. "School counselors and administrators are on-site and available to provide support and answer questions from families and scholars."
 Advertisement Advertisement Carter is reportedly being held in the Montgomery County Detention Facility on a $300,000 bond. It is unclear if he has yet entered a plea or retained an attorney to speak on his behalf.
